tables.name: account
tables.label: Account
tables.description: > > This table holds information on all available accounts.

columns.name: totp_secret
columns.label: Totp secret
columns.description:
The authenticator key.

Key can be generated through the Google Authenticator API, a 3rd-party TOTP generator, or manually specified.
[Implementation link on Wikipedia](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Authenticator#Implementations) for the Google Authenticator API

columns.name: email
columns.label: Email
columns.hint: The e-mail address associated with this account.
columns.description: The e-mail address associated with this account.

columns.name: reg_mail
columns.label: Reg mail
columns.hint: The registration e-mail address associated with this account.
columns.description: The registration e-mail address associated with this account.

columns.name: joindate
columns.label: Joindate
columns.hint: The Unix timestamp when the account was created.
columns.description: The Unix timestamp when the account was created.

columns.name: last_ip
columns.label: Last ip
columns.hint: The last IP used by the person who logged in the account.
columns.description: The last IP used by the person who logged in the account.

columns.name: last_attempt_ip
columns.label: Last attempt ip
columns.hint: The last IP used by the person who tried to log into the account.
columns.description: The last IP used by the person who tried to log into the account.

columns.name: failed_logins
columns.label: Failed logins
columns.hint: The number of failed logins attempted on the account.
columns.description: The number of failed logins attempted on the account.

columns.name: locked
columns.label: Locked
columns.hint: Controlls if the account has been locked to it's last IP.
columns.description:
Controlls if the account has been locked to it's last IP. This can be controlled with the `.account lock` command.
The `.ban account` command does not lock it.
* 0: the user can log in from any IP, and their **last_ip** will be updated if it is different
* 1: the user can only log in with their **last_ip**.

columns.name: lock_country
columns.label: Lock country
columns.hint: A country code from IP2Location worldserver.conf IPLocationFile needs to point to the table fom the service above for this feature to be enabled.
columns.description:
A country code from [IP2Location](https://lite.ip2location.com/database/ip-country)

worldserver.conf [`IPLocationFile`](https://trinitycore.info/en/files/configuration/home) needs to point to the table fom the service above for this feature to be enabled.

columns.name: last_login
columns.label: Last login
columns.hint: The Unix timestamp when the account was last logged into.
columns.description: The Unix timestamp when the account was last logged into.

columns.name: online
columns.label: Online
columns.hint: Signifies if the account is currently logged in and online.
columns.description:
Signifies if the account is currently logged in and online.
* 0: offline
* 1: online

columns.name: expansion
columns.label: Expansion
columns.hint: Integer 0 – 2 controlling if the client logged in on the account has any expansions.
columns.description: Integer 0 – 2 controlling if the client logged in on the account has any expansions. (for example if client is TBC, but expansion is set to 0, it will not be able to enter outlands and etc.)

columns.name: mutetime
columns.label: Mutetime
columns.hint: The Unix timestamp, when the account will be unmuted.
columns.description:
The Unix timestamp, when the account will be unmuted.

To see when mute will be expired you can use this query:
```sql
SELECT FROM_UNIXTIME(`mutetime`) FROM `account`;
```

columns.name: muteby
columns.label: Muteby
columns.hint: The character name with the rights to the .mute command that give the mute.
columns.description: The character name with the rights to the `.mute` command that give the mute.

columns.name: locale
columns.label: Locale
columns.hint: The locale used by the client logged into this account.
columns.description:
The locale used by the client logged into this account. If multiple locale data has been configured and added to the world servers, the world servers will return the proper locale strings to the client.

See [Localization](/how-to/localization):

columns.name: os
columns.label: Os
columns.description:
Stores information about client's OS. Used by Warden system.
* `Win`
* `Mac`

columns.name: recruiter
columns.label: Recruiter
columns.hint: The account id of another account.
columns.description: The [account id](#id) of another account. Used for recuit-a-friend system.

tables.name: account_access
tables.label: Account access
tables.description: > This table holds security access level for any realm in [realmlist](../auth/realmlist#id) table.

columns.name: SecurityLevel
columns.label: Security Level
columns.description:
The account security level. Different levels have access to different commands. 
The individual level required for a command is defined in the [command table](../world/command) in each realm.

columns.name: RealmID
columns.label: Realm ID
columns.description:
The [realm id](../auth/realmlist#id).

`-1` applies the rights to all realms.

columns.name: Comment
columns.label: Comment
columns.hint: This field is for any comment you want to make.
columns.description: This field is for any comment you want to make. It is arbitrary text.

tables.name: account_banned
tables.label: Account banned
tables.description: > This table lists all of the accounts that have been banned along with the date when (or if) the ban will expire.

columns.name: bandate
columns.label: Bandate
columns.hint: Unix timestamp when the account was banned.
columns.description: Unix timestamp when the account was banned.

columns.name: unbandate
columns.label: Unbandate
columns.hint: Unix timestamp when the account will be automatically unbanned.
columns.description:
Unix timestamp when the account will be automatically unbanned. 
If **unbandate** is equal to **bandate** this is a permanent ban.

columns.name: bannedby
columns.label: Bannedby
columns.hint: The name of the character executing the .ban command.
columns.description: The name of the character executing the `.ban` command.

columns.name: active
columns.label: Active
columns.hint: Controls if the ban is currently active or not.
columns.description:
Controls if the ban is currently active or not.
* 0: ban expired
* 1: ban is active

tables.name: account_muted
tables.label: Account muted
tables.description: > This table lists all of the accounts that have been muted along with the date when the mute will expire.

columns.name: mutedate
columns.label: Mutedate
columns.hint: Unix timestamp when the account was muted.
columns.description: Unix timestamp when the account was muted.

columns.name: mutedby
columns.label: Mutedby
columns.hint: The name of the character executing the .mute command.
columns.description: The name of the character executing the `.mute` command.

tables.name: autobroadcast
tables.label: Autobroadcast
tables.description: > This table contains the autobroadcast entries for your realms.  > Values like it's activity, position and Timer (\*.On, \*.Center, \*.Timer) are defined within the [worldserver.conf](https://trinitycore.info/en/files/configuration/home). They are chosen randomly, based on their weight.

columns.name: realmid
columns.label: Realmid
columns.hint: The realm id defines which realm this entry belongs to.
columns.description:
The [realm id](../auth/realmlist#id) defines which realm this entry belongs to.

Use `-1` for all realms to load this entry.

columns.name: id
columns.label: Id
columns.description: Unique identifier key per realm. Entries with same id will override each other without warnings - this can be used to replace `-1` **realmid** entry on a specific realm.

columns.name: weight
columns.label: Weight
columns.description: A non-negative integer. Entries with higher weight have more chance to get picked.

columns.name: text
columns.label: Text
columns.description: The text to broadcast. [UI escape sequences](https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/UI_escape_sequences?oldid=1972918) can be used.

columns.name: guid
columns.label: Guid
columns.hint: The battle pet global unique identifier.
columns.description: The battle pet global unique identifier.

values.name: Favorite
values.comment: Marked as favorite in battle pet journal

values.name: Ability0Selection
values.comment: Selected second ability of ability slot 0

values.name: Ability1Selection
values.comment: Selected second ability of ability slot 1

values.name: Ability2Selection
values.comment: Selected second ability of ability slot 2

values.name: FanfareNeeded
values.comment: Shown as a present in battle pet journal

columns.name: name
columns.label: Name
columns.description: Current battle pet name. If empty, the battle pet will use the [name](../world/creature_template#name) of the creature associated with the [species](#species).

tables.name: realmlist
tables.label: Realmlist
tables.description: > This table sets up information on all available realms. Each row controls a different realm.

columns.name: id
columns.label: Id
columns.description: The realm ID. This number is unique for every realm and it MUST correlate with the RealmID configuration value in worldserver.conf.

columns.name: name
columns.label: Name
columns.description: The name of the realm. This will appear in the realm selection list as well as in the character selection screen.

columns.name: address
columns.label: Address
columns.hint: The public (WAN) or LAN IP address of the world server.
columns.description:
The public (WAN) or LAN IP address of the world server. Use 127.0.0.1 in this field if only you is connecting to the server (and it runs on the same machine as your client).

Alternatively you can use a domain name like *example.com*.

columns.name: port
columns.label: Port
columns.hint: The port that the world server is running on.
columns.description: The port that the world server is running on. If all world servers are on the same machine, they will all need to use a different port.

columns.name: timezone
columns.label: Timezone
columns.hint: The realm timezone, it will be displayed in the tabs of the realmlist.
columns.description:
The realm timezone, it will be displayed in the tabs of the realmlist.

**timezone** corresponds to [cfg_categories IDs](/files/DBC/335/cfg_categories#id)

columns.name: allowedSecurityLevel
columns.label: Allowed Security Level
columns.hint: The minimum SecurityLevel required for accounts to log in to this realm.
columns.description:
The minimum [SecurityLevel](../auth/account_access#securitylevel) required for accounts to log in to this realm.

Changing this value will automatically update the visible in-game realm list, but the Worldserver must be restarted for it to truly take effect.

columns.name: population
columns.label: Population
columns.hint: This field is automatically updated at regular intervals and will have the current population.
columns.description:
This field is automatically updated at regular intervals and will have the current population.

The formula to calculate the value in this field is: `playerCount / maxPlayerCount * 2`.
In the realm list in-game, the thresholds for low, medium, and high population are 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 respectively.

columns.name: gamebuild
columns.label: Gamebuild
columns.hint: Accepted Client version for the realm.
columns.description: Accepted Client version for the realm.
